title: What a shooting ground looks like
summary: The clubhouse, the Sporting™ layouts, the Compak® Sporting field and the traps: what you will see on your first visit.

body.html: A shooting ground, often just called “the ground”, usually has a clubhouse with registration, a café and gun racks, practice fields and the courses used for competitions.

For Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ the ground is divided into layouts: groups of shooting stands from which one round of 25 targets is shot. Traps are often hidden behind bushes or in ditches, or set on towers. Targets then fly the way game (the birds and hares that hunters shoot) would: over a field, out of trees, over water. How a layout and a round work: How a Sporting™ layout and round work.

A Sporting™ stand is a 1 m square or a circle 1 m across. It should be level where possible and must not be slippery, because this is a safety matter. In front of the stand you will find the target menu: it lists the traps in shooting order and any special targets.

Compak® Sporting is set up on one field with 6 traps lettered A to F and 5 shooting stations in a line. Each station is 1 × 1 m, with 2–5 m between the centres of neighbouring stations. Traps can stand in front of or beside the stations; a trap behind them sits on a tower at least 4 m high. Each station has a firing angle limiter, a frame that stops the gun swinging in an unsafe direction. More: How a Compak® Sporting layout works.

Targets come in several types: standard, midi, mini (also called super mini), battue (thin and flat), rabbit (it rolls along the ground) and flash. A flash target leaves a bright puff of powder when hit. The colour is chosen so the target stands out against the sky or the trees.

On your first visit, look at the signs and markings: where you may walk, where spectators stand and where shooting is allowed. Each ground has its own rules, so ask for them before your first shot. The basic safety habits are in The core safety rules.

key_points.html: A Sporting™ layout is a group of stands over natural ground.
A Sporting™ stand is a 1 m square or a circle 1 m across, level and not slippery.
Compak® Sporting: one field with 6 traps lettered A to F and 5 shooting stations in a line, and a firing angle limiter at each station.
Read the target menu at each stand, and learn the ground rules before you shoot.

did_you_know.html: A flash target holds bright powder, so a hit shows even from far away. Spectators love it.
